topic: Linear Transformations and Matrices: The Geometry of Change

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Coordinates
lecture_lines: Vectors are arrows in a 2D plane.
Point (x, y) uses basis vectors i-hat and j-hat.
Any vector is a linear combination of basis vectors.
animations: Display coordinate grid with origin at center using #FFFFFF.
Highlight basis vectors i and j with #FF0000 and #00FF00.
Show vector v as a linear combination of i and j with #FFFF00.

sections.title: Defining Linear Transformation
lecture_lines: Linear transformations move vectors within space.
The origin point must remain fixed.
Grid lines must remain parallel and evenly spaced.
animations: Fade in empty transformation plane with grid #FFFFFF.
Draw grid lines transforming into a new orientation #FFFF00.
Label the transformed space with clear identifier #00FFFF.

sections.title: The Matrix as a Transformation Recipe
lecture_lines: Matrices track where basis vectors i-hat and j-hat land.
Columns define the destination of basis vectors.
All points transform based on these new basis positions.
Linear combinations map the entire space.
animations: Display a standard 2x2 matrix as a transformation recipe #FFFFFF.
Animate i vector moving to the first column vector #FF0000.
Animate j vector moving to the second column vector #00FF00.
Highlight how linear combinations map the entire space #FFFF00.

sections.title: Visualizing Composition
lecture_lines: Matrix multiplication applies two transformations sequentially.
Order of operations significantly changes the final result.
Rotation then shear differs from shear then rotation.
animations: Show two distinct transformation grids side-by-side #FFFFFF.
Animate the sequence of applying one transformation after another #FFFF00.
Highlight the resulting composite transformation output #00FFFF.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Matrices are the engine behind modern computer graphics.
Games use linear transformations to render 3D worlds.
Dynamic matrix values move characters in real-time.
